entries.name: Set lining
entries.regs_verbatim: Set lining: only permitted in the lakes of Zone A (see tables for exclusions). One line, single hook, gap not less than 3 cm, marked with the angler's name, address and telephone number. Any game fish that you catch other than burbot must be released.

entries.name: White sturgeon — SARA
entries.regs_verbatim: White Sturgeon in the Omineca Region. White Sturgeon from the Nechako and the Upper Fraser watersheds are listed as endangered under the Species at Risk Act (SARA). It is illegal to fish for, kill, harm, or harass SARA-listed White Sturgeon in the Upper Fraser and Nechako Rivers.

rules.verbatim: It is illegal to fish for, kill, harm, or harass SARA-listed White Sturgeon in the Upper Fraser and Nechako Rivers.
rules.review_reason: Held to Region 7A (the page's heading: 'White Sturgeon in the Omineca Region'). Bound to the whole Fraser and Nechako before, it closed the lower Fraser's catch-and-release sturgeon fishery in Regions 2, 3 and 5 with superior authority. The Upper Fraser population's lower end below Region 7A, and the upper Nechako in Region 6, are for a curator.

entries.name: Omineca tagging studies
entries.regs_verbatim: NOTICE TO ANGLERS The Ministry and it's partners are conducting several tagging studies on a variety of species throughout the Omineca region. Some tags offer cash rewards for reporting. If you catch a fish with a coloured "spaghetti" tag, whether you retain it or release it, please report the tag number, tag colour, date, time and location prior to releasing the fish. To report your catch of a tagged fish please contact the Fish and Wildlife Regional Office in Prince George at (250) 614-7400.

entries.name: Stocked lakes
entries.scope_note: RECOVERED — the tables list only stocked lakes that ALSO carry water-specific rules, so the 'Stocked' symbol under-counts by design.
entries.regs_verbatim: 54 lakes in the Omineca region are currently stocked with Rainbow trout, Eastern Brook trout, and/or Kokanee. The water-specific regulations tables identify only stocked lakes with waterbody specific regulations.
